I checked the validator source: it already excludes shared finger-base vertices, so my earlier base-seam explanation is not supported. I am diagnosing actual distal collisions and adding geometric separation while retaining the image fit. A two-second free object rest moves 0.027mm and settles; no initial penetration.

The 15mm distal bone separation reduces self-intersection fraction from 0.87 to 0.053, with left mask IoU 0.752 and opposed-grasp 0.970 retained; object penetration passes. Remaining crossings are mostly adjacent index/middle and middle/ring fingers. Measuring the fitted MANO skin around its bones gives p95 radii 9–9.5mm for long fingers and12.5mm for thumb, larger than my capsule prior. Next fit uses19mm long-finger and23mm thumb-to-finger separation, derived from those skin radii. No validation threshold is changed.

Contact ends341, left active coverage271/272, frame255invalid under unchanged IoU0.5 rule. The final reconstruction minutes will test a local250–260MANO refit with all other frames and shape frozen. It must improve observed fit without introducing collisions; otherwise v2 remains the reference. Training simulation starts only after10:56:21Z.

The local frame255 refit raises its mask IoU only from0.4364to0.4425, still below the unchanged0.5validity rule; it is not retained. Freezing unrelated frames and shape was verified exactly. An exact-symmetry branch experiment preserves cube geometry (Hausdorff error0), but only reduces the frame110step from49.88to45.74deg and leaves the continuity warning; no material-axis evidence improves, so v2 remains the recorded reference. These failures sharpen its limitations rather than justify invented states. Remaining reconstruction minutes audit the measured hand/wrist/contact quantities and reproducibility before the strict10:56:21Ztransition.

Final reference audit before the 60-minute boundary: every source frame has exactly one detailed event, source video hash matches, camera-to-object composition is exact, replay discrepancy is only1.39e-7from float32rotation-to-quaternion normalization. Nominal cube clearance during the active skill stays above the mat, while release/tumbling is correctly separated. Wrist median speed0.0568m/s and angular speed0.819rad/s; palm-normal median68.34degfrom up; wrist-to-cube centre median0.1317m. Geometric cube angular-speed spikes remain ambiguous with layer motion and symmetry, so the policy should use the reconstructed contact roles/posture plus TASK.mdexact quarter-turn goals, not imitate those spikes as ground truth. Reference remains r0007/v2.

After the required60minutes, criteria v1 is recorded (r0011). Simulation construction begins now. Initial URDF import discarded the static palm/root masses (0.4005kg), which would violate hwspec1.3L. A local URDF copy adds a floating root and disables fixed-link fusion; imported mass is now exactly0.7088kg. Installed specifications/models are untouched. The cube mechanism will use passive contact-coupled articulated corners; no object actuators or request-dependent mechanics. Primitive feasibility, including wrong-turn and integrity failures, must be demonstrated before task PPO.

Nominal pad-contact geometry is collision-free enough, but arbitrary inward position preload ejects the cube. A friction-cone wrench calculation at the actual pad contacts finds gravity support feasible with less than1Nnormal load, so the failure is force distribution rather than missing torque capacity. I am testing hand-PD position offsets corresponding to balanced contact forces (J-transpose mapped through prescribed gains), with no forces applied to the cube. Separately, an object-only clamped-core bench couples a driven corner to the other three corners for ±90degree turns about all three axes (max corner error2.1–3.7degrees, penetration<0.15mm). That diagnostic uses external torques and is NOT hand feasibility.
